reasoning: Verified live code before decomposing: PlatformWrite/OptionalDepUpdate are 2-field structs at plan.rs:45-55; plan_version hardcodes both to Vec::new() at version.rs:262-263; apply.rs's platform_writes loop (244-252) has no precondition and active_ecosystems (325-349) only reads plan.bumps. GroupMember::PlatformManifest{owner,role,path,name} lives at config/groups.rs:26-33 and is only populated via IdentityIndex.platform, itself populated in walk.rs:190-216 by detecting npm package.json files with non-empty os+cpu arrays (detect_npm_role, walk.rs:590+) during the walk -- so a realistic test fixture for a Fixed group with a PlatformManifest member is: an owner Cargo crate + a sibling npm package.json declaring os/cpu arrays, referenced by its own npm name in [[fixed-group]] members. Manifest reads go through callisto_manifests::open(&ManifestDecl::new(path, ManifestRole::Canonical, fmt), &OpenContext) exactly as apply.rs already does at 118-136/244-262 -- OpenContext derivation is duplicated verbatim into plan_version rather than extracted into a shared helper, since the spec's api_surface explicitly describes plan_version deriving it itself and extracting a helper is an unrequested refactor. Every task's covers_criteria was cross-checked against all 16 IDs (AC-001..AC-013 + AC-002b, AC-007b, AC-012b) at the end -- all 16 present.

tasks.commit_message:
feat(graph): add `from` field to PlatformWrite

Captures the platform manifest's on-disk version at plan time so apply_version_plan can precondition-check it before writing, mirroring PlannedBump.from's role in the sibling bump loops.

tasks.title: plan_version: OpenContext derivation + core platform_writes producer (single platform member, happy path)
tasks.reasoning: This is the core producer logic: for each Fixed group's GroupMember::PlatformManifest whose owner received a real PlannedBump this run, open the platform manifest (ManifestRole::Canonical unconditionally, OpenContext derived exactly as apply.rs:118-130 does) and emit a PlatformWrite with from=on-disk current_version, version=owner's bump target. Also covers the two 'no write should happen' regressions (AC-005: no platform members anywhere; AC-006: owner not bumped) since they exercise the same new code path with zero/no-match inputs and share the test fixture helpers already in this file's `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (git_init_with_commit, tag, commit_all).

test.description: Three tests added to commands/version.rs's existing test module, reusing its git_init_with_commit/tag/commit_all helpers. Platform manifest fixtures use a Cargo owner package plus a sibling npm package.json with non-empty os/cpu arrays (the only mechanism, per walk.rs:590-630, that causes IdentityIndex to register a GroupMember::PlatformManifest), referenced in [[fixed-group]] members by its own npm package name.
test.expected_failure: plan_version_emits_platform_write_for_bumped_owner_with_platform_sibling fails: assertion `left == right` failed: expected exactly one PlatformWrite, got: [] (plan_version currently hardcodes platform_writes to Vec::new()). The other two tests pass trivially before implementation since Vec::new() is already empty -- they exist to pin the regression once the producer logic is added.

implementation.description: Replace the hardcoded `platform_writes: Vec::new()` with real producer logic, driven by Fixed-group PlatformManifest members whose owner has an entry in the `bumps` vector already computed earlier in this function.
steps: Add `use crate::config::groups::{GroupMember, GroupMemberKind};` to the top of crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs.

Immediately before the `Ok(VersionPlan { ... })` return at the end of plan_version, derive cargo_workspace/npm_workspace_kind/OpenContext exactly as apply.rs:118-130 does, then loop over ws.config.groups.fixed.values() -> group.members(GroupMemberKind::PlatformManifest), and for each owner with an entry in bump_by_pkg, open the manifest via ManifestFormat::from_path + ManifestDecl::new(path, ManifestRole::Canonical, fmt) + callisto_manifests::open(&decl, &open_ctx), read current_version(), and push a PlatformWrite { manifest: path.clone(), version: bump.to.clone(), from: current }.

Change the VersionPlan struct literal's `platform_writes: Vec::new(),` to `platform_writes,` (the newly computed variable). Leave `optional_dep_updates: Vec::new(),` untouched for this task -- Task 5 replaces it.

tasks.expected_pass: all tests pass, including the three new tests

plan_version now walks Fixed-group PlatformManifest members whose owner has a real PlannedBump this run, reads each platform manifest's current on-disk version via the same OpenContext derivation apply_version_plan already uses, and emits a PlatformWrite carrying both from and target version -- closing the previously hardcoded Vec::new() gap.

tasks.reasoning: Task 2's implementation already derives cargo_workspace inheritance into OpenContext and opens manifests via ManifestRole::Canonical regardless of format, so a `version.workspace = true` Cargo platform manifest and multiple platform siblings under one owner both flow through the same code path with zero additional implementation. This task adds tests only, pinning that these two scenarios genuinely work end-to-end through plan_version's real return value (not a direct current_version() call in isolation, per AC-002b's wording).

test.description: Two tests: AC-002b (maturin-style Cargo platform manifest inheriting version.workspace = true from the root [workspace.package] version) and AC-007 (owner with two platform siblings, both must appear).

This task exists purely to pin the two scenarios with dedicated tests, per the spec's explicit call-out that both must be proven through plan_version's actual return value.
steps: No production code changes. If either test fails, the bug is in Task 2's implementation (loop only processing the first PlatformManifest member found, or cargo_workspace being derived as None instead of from WorkspaceCargoResolver) -- fix that code in commands/version.rs rather than adding new code here.

tasks.title: plan_version platform_writes: AC-008 error propagation on unreadable platform manifest
tasks.reasoning: Task 2's implementation already uses `?` on ManifestFormat::from_path, ManifestDecl::new, callisto_manifests::open, and current_version() -- all of which already propagate as GraphError. This test proves that end-to-end: a platform manifest that validated during the walk (so it is a real GroupMember::PlatformManifest) but is deleted from disk before plan_version runs must surface as Err, not panic and not a partial VersionPlan.

Since this task depends on Task 2, in practice this test is written and should pass immediately once Task 2 is merged -- if it does not, Task 2's `?` propagation has a gap and must be fixed there.

steps: No production code changes required. If the test fails, fix the propagation gap in Task 2's loop in commands/version.rs (commonly: a `.ok()` or `.unwrap_or_default()` silently swallowing the error instead of `?`).

tasks.title: plan_version: optional_dep_updates producer (single platform member)
tasks.reasoning: Extends the same group/member loop from Task 2: for each platform member whose owner was bumped, additionally open the owner's own canonical manifest and check via iter_dependencies() whether an existing DepKind::Optional entry matches the platform member's name. Only when a match exists is an OptionalDepUpdate produced -- never speculatively created (AC-004).

test.description: AC-003 (owner has a matching optionalDependencies entry -> update produced) and AC-004 (owner has no matching entry -> nothing produced) as two tests.
test.expected_failure: plan_version_emits_optional_dep_update_when_owner_declares_matching_optional_dep fails: assertion `left == right` failed: got: [] (optional_dep_updates is still hardcoded to Vec::new() before this task's implementation lands).

implementation.description: Extend the loop added in Task 2 to also detect a matching optional dependency on the owner's canonical manifest and accumulate updates per owner-manifest-path (using a BTreeMap so multiple platform siblings under the same owner naturally merge, which Task 6 pins).
steps: In the same loop from Task 2, also bind `name` from the GroupMember::PlatformManifest destructure.
Before the loop, add a `BTreeMap<PathBuf, Vec<(String, Version)>>` accumulator for optional dep updates.

Inside the loop, after computing `bump`, open the owner's canonical manifest and check via iter_dependencies() whether a DepKind::Optional entry matches `name`; if so, push (name, bump.to) into the accumulator keyed by the owner's manifest path.
After the loop, convert the accumulator into Vec<OptionalDepUpdate> and assign it to the VersionPlan struct literal's `optional_dep_updates` field, replacing `Vec::new()`.

When a Fixed group's owner package declares an existing optionalDependencies entry matching a bumped platform-manifest sibling's name, plan_version now emits an OptionalDepUpdate targeting that entry -- never speculatively creating one that didn't already exist.

tasks.title: apply.rs Fix 1: extend active_ecosystems to platform_writes and optional_dep_updates manifest paths
tasks.reasoning: active_ecosystems (apply.rs:325-349) currently only derives from plan.bumps, so a plan with only platform_writes/optional_dep_updates populated (bumps empty) never stages the npm lockfile even though an npm manifest was touched. This task extends the same active_ecosystems HashSet-building expression to also fold in plan.platform_writes and plan.optional_dep_updates manifest paths via ManifestFormat::from_path(...).ecosystem(). This task is independent of Tasks 1-6 (different file, does not touch PlatformWrite's fields) and independent of Task 8 (no precondition logic involved) -- it can be built and merged in any order relative to them.

test.description: AC-009 (platform_writes-only plan stages the npm lockfile, no refresh), AC-010 (same for optional_dep_updates-only plan), AC-011 (bumps-only plan behavior is a byte-for-byte regression -- already covered by every pre-existing apply.rs test in this file, which all currently pass and must continue to pass unmodified).
test.expected_failure: Both tests fail: `assert!(outcome.staged.contains(...))` fails because active_ecosystems is currently derived only from plan.bumps (empty in both plans), so Ecosystem::Npm is never in the set and the lockfile is skipped in the staging loop at apply.rs:423-431.

implementation.description: Extend the active_ecosystems HashSet-building code (apply.rs:325-349) to also fold in manifest paths from plan.platform_writes and plan.optional_dep_updates.
steps: In crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs, chain two additional filter_map iterators onto the existing active_ecosystems collect(): one over plan.platform_writes mapping each pw.manifest through ManifestFormat::from_path(...).ok().map(|fmt| fmt.ecosystem()), and one over plan.optional_dep_updates doing the same for opt.manifest.

No other code changes -- the existing lockfile_ecosystems staging table (apply.rs:412-422) and refresh-subprocess logic (apply.rs:354-408) are untouched, since npm has no refresh subprocess and Cargo/Pypi refresh triggers stay scoped to plan.bumps-driven ecosystems only.

tasks.expected_pass: all tests pass, including all pre-existing apply.rs tests (proving AC-011's byte-for-byte regression requirement)
tasks.commit_message:
fix(graph): stage npm lockfile when a plan touches only platform_writes or optional_dep_updates

active_ecosystems previously derived exclusively from plan.bumps, so a plan containing only platform-manifest or optional-dependency writes never staged the npm lockfile. Extends the derivation to also consult those two fields' manifest paths.

tasks.title: apply.rs Fix 2: platform_writes dispatch loop precondition check
tasks.reasoning: The platform_writes dispatch loop (apply.rs:244-252) currently writes unconditionally with no precondition check, unlike the sibling bump loops which already check current==from/current==target/else. This task adds the same three-way branch using PlatformWrite.from (added in Task 1), returning GraphError::UnexpectedManifestVersion on drift, treating current==target as idempotent-retry success.

test.description: Three tests: AC-012 (drift -- current is neither from nor target -> Err(UnexpectedManifestVersion) with correct fields, manifest not written), AC-012b (current already equals target -> Ok, no re-write, but path still pushed to staged), AC-013 (current equals from, the ordinary case -> succeeds, on-disk version becomes target -- this is the pre-existing test from apply.rs:2240, already updated with a matching `from` in Task 1, and must continue to pass unmodified as the regression proof).
test.expected_failure: platform_write_drift_returns_unexpected_manifest_version_and_leaves_manifest_untouched fails: `apply_version_plan` currently succeeds unconditionally (writes 1.1.0 over the drifted 9.9.9), so `result` is `Ok(..)` not `Err(UnexpectedManifestVersion)`, and the manifest is NOT unchanged. platform_write_idempotent_retry_when_already_at_target_succeeds_without_rewrite happens to pass even before the fix (current unconditional-write behavior also succeeds here), but is included to pin AC-012b's exact non-error semantics once the precondition check exists.

implementation.description: Add the same three-way current==from/current==to/else branch the sibling bump loops already use, to the platform_writes dispatch loop.
steps: In crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs, in the platform_writes loop (currently around lines 244-252), after opening the handle, read current_version(), then branch: if current == pw.version, skip the write (idempotent retry) but still push to modified_paths; else if current == pw.from, write_version + persist as before; else, return Err(GraphError::UnexpectedManifestVersion { path: pw.manifest.clone(), expected_from: pw.from.clone(), expected_to: pw.version.clone(), found: current }).

tasks.expected_pass: all tests pass, including the pre-existing apply_version_plan_executes_platform_writes_and_optional_dep_updates test (proving AC-013's non-drifted regression path)
tasks.commit_message:
fix(graph): add current-version precondition check to platform_writes dispatch loop

apply_version_plan previously wrote platform manifests unconditionally, unlike the sibling bump loops. Adds the same current==from/current==to/else precondition, returning UnexpectedManifestVersion on drift and treating current==to as a safe idempotent-retry success.
